newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates mixed, supply good.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates mixed, supply good.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were mixed on Monday amid good supply after the central bank's cut in the reserve ratio by one percentage point, dealers said.
"Some of the funds that were tied up in mandatory reserves may already have gone back to the banks," one dealer told Reuters.
But the banking sector slightly increased its borrowing from the central bank to 104.5 million kuna in Lombard loans. They are granted at 9.5 percent.
There was 60 million kuna surplus in money market trade after 22.8 million kuna was settled by midmorning. Lack of two-month funds left one bank short.
Call money loans were made mostly at 10.5 percent, though one foreign bank reduced its rate to 9.0 percent.
Banks charged 10.5 percent for three-day loans and a steady 11 percent for one-week funds. One savings bank paid a higher 19 percent for a two-month deal.
Overnight trade over the weekend totalled 55 million kuna which went to nine banks for their mandatory reserves. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
